description:
## Finding

The \`realistic-demo-ids\` cargo feature has two API-contract gaps
on different axes.

### Gap A: undocumented in lib.rs //! doc

\`Cargo.toml\` declares the feature at line 32 with an inline
comment, and \`memory.rs:187\` documents the behavior change on
\`demo_next_id\`. But the crate-level \`//!\` doc in \`src/lib.rs\`
(which is what a consumer scans first when browsing the rendered
docs) does NOT mention the feature.

The \`memory\` feature gets its own heading at lib.rs:19-27 with
purpose, \"Not production\" caveat, and pre-1.0 stability note.
\`realistic-demo-ids\` gets nothing. A consumer reading the rustdoc
top-of-crate page does not learn the feature exists, what it
does, or whether to activate it.

### Gap B: behavior-altering feature on an unchanged pub fn signature

\`MemoryBackend::demo_next_id\` (memory.rs:200) has the same
signature in both feature modes:

```rust
fn demo_next_id(inner: &mut Inner, type_name: &'static str, account_id: &str) -> Id
```

The runtime output shape changes (\`memory.rs:187-200\`):

- feature OFF (default): deterministic, \`format!(\"{n:016x}\")\` based on inner len
- feature ON: timestamp+counter, mail-server-style

Per Cargo features guidance, behavioral feature flags that mutate
the *output* of an unchanged function signature are a known
unification hazard:

- Crate A's tests activate \`realistic-demo-ids\` for realism
- Crate B's tests consume \`MemoryBackend\` expecting deterministic ids
- Cargo's feature unification means \`realistic-demo-ids\` is ON
  for *both* crates in the unified workspace build
- B's tests silently break

\`MemoryBackend\` is documented as not-production so the blast
radius is bounded, but the unification hazard is real for
test-helper consumption across a multi-crate workspace.

## Why this matters more than ordinary feature docs gaps

\`realistic-demo-ids\` is a feature on a public function that
mutates the function's observable output without changing its
signature. The cargo features convention is that features should
either be (a) additive on the API surface or (b) clearly
documented as runtime-behavior-altering and not unification-safe.
Here the runtime-altering aspect is documented in memory.rs but
not at the crate-level entry point.

## Recommendation

Two things:

1. Add a \`# realistic-demo-ids feature\` heading to lib.rs's \`//!\`
   doc, modelled on the existing \`# memory feature\` heading at
   lines 19-27. Explain what the feature does, its interaction
   with \`memory\`, and warn that the output format of
   \`demo_next_id\` is feature-dependent and must not be relied on
   across dep-graph configurations.

2. Add a rustdoc note on \`demo_next_id\` itself (memory.rs:187)
   reinforcing the unification hazard: \"The output format
   depends on the \`realistic-demo-ids\` feature, which is
   unified across the dep graph by cargo. Crates that depend on
   a specific format MUST NOT rely on the absence of the feature.\"

## Engineering basis

- Verified Cargo.toml line 32: \`realistic-demo-ids = []\`
- Verified \`grep -n \"realistic-demo-ids\" crate-jmap-chat-server/src/lib.rs\`
  returns zero hits. The feature is genuinely absent from lib.rs.
- Verified \`grep -n \"realistic-demo-ids\" crate-jmap-chat-server/src/memory.rs\`
  returns 4 hits at lines 187/195/201/220 documenting and gating the
  behavior.
- Verified the \`demo_next_id\` function signature at memory.rs:200
  is identical under both \`#[cfg(feature = ...)]\` arms.
title: API contract: realistic-demo-ids feature is undocumented in lib.rs //! AND behavior-altering on pub fn demo_next_id
